label: Linux host
summary: CPU busy and steal, memory, swap, OOM kills, disk latency, filesystems, network
source: node_exporter (prometheus/node_exporter) default collectors (cpu, loadavg, meminfo, vmstat, diskstats, filesystem, netdev, netstat, filefd, stat), names read at master on 2026-10-08. Tools' names checked the same day against Telegraf's cpu, mem, kernel_vmstat, kernel and diskio inputs, Datadog's system, disk and oom_kill integrations, the OpenTelemetry hostmetrics scrapers' documentation, and the CloudWatch agent's Linux metric list (namespace CWAgent). Busy is everything but idle, so iowait and steal count as busy; Telegraf's usage_active is that (cpu.go: total minus idle) and needs report_active = true. AWS/EC2 CPUUtilization is not named: it is the hypervisor's view, not the guest's CPU busy. OTel's system.cpu.utilization is off by default, and is named for steal only, so one file holds one series under that name. Bands are not shipped for CPU, memory or disk: the right number depends on the machine and on whether the test means to saturate it. Nor for NIC errors and drops, the research's warn > 0 included: rx_dropped also counts packets of an unsupported protocol and those L2 filtering discards (rtnl_link_stats64 in include/uapi/linux/if_link.h), so a healthy host's rate need not be 0.

metrics.name: cpu.busy.pct
metrics.label: CPU busy (%)
metrics.description: Time the CPUs were not idle, averaged over the cores; iowait and steal count as busy. Response times climb as it nears 100 %, because run queues form.

telegraf.note: needs report_active = true in inputs.cpu; tag cpu=cpu-total

cloudwatch.note: needs the CloudWatch agent; the cpu-total series, statistic Average. Not AWS/EC2 CPUUtilization, the hypervisor's view

metrics.name: cpu.iowait.pct
metrics.label: CPU iowait (%)
metrics.description: CPU time spent idle while waiting for disk. A rise under load points at storage rather than compute; the disk metrics judge it better.

cloudwatch.note: needs the CloudWatch agent; the cpu-total series, statistic Average

metrics.name: cpu.steal.pct
metrics.label: CPU steal (%)
metrics.description: Time the VM wanted a CPU and the hypervisor gave it to another tenant. High steal means the run measured the host, not your system.

otel.note: off by default: enable it in the hostmetrics cpu scraper; state=steal, averaged over cpu

cloudwatch.note: needs the CloudWatch agent; the cpu-total series, statistic Average

metrics.name: load.per.core
metrics.label: Load per core
metrics.description: The 1-minute load average divided by the number of CPUs: runnable and disk-blocked tasks per core. Above 1 work is queueing; it lags the load, and disk alone can raise it.

metrics.name: memory.available.pct
metrics.label: Memory available (%)
metrics.description: Memory the kernel can hand out without swapping (MemAvailable), as a percentage of the total. Falling toward 0 comes before swapping and OOM kills.

cloudwatch.note: needs the CloudWatch agent; statistic Minimum

metrics.name: swap.pages.rate
metrics.label: Swap in + out (pages/s)
metrics.description: Pages swapped in and out per second. Any sustained swapping turns memory pressure into disk latency.

metrics.name: oom.kills
metrics.label: OOM kills per minute (peak)
metrics.description: Processes the kernel killed to free memory, in any minute of the run. A worker died, and the client results may show it only as errors.

datadog.note: needs the system-probe OOM Kill check (eBPF, kernel 4.9 or later)

metrics.name: disk.busy.pct
metrics.label: Disk busy (%)
metrics.description: Share of time the busiest device had I/O in flight (iostat %util). On NVMe and EBS it can read 100 with headroom left, so judge disk latency instead.

telegraf.note: one series per device (tag name): export the max per host

datadog.note: one series per device: export the max by host

otel.note: seconds, one series per device: keep the device in the instance column

cloudwatch.note: needs the CloudWatch agent; milliseconds, statistic Sum, one series per device (name)

metrics.name: disk.await.ms
metrics.label: Disk latency, await (ms)
metrics.description: Average time an I/O spends queued and served on the slowest device: the disk's share of a slow response.

telegraf.note: one series per device (tag name): export the max per host

datadog.note: one series per device: export the max by host

metrics.name: disk.queue.depth
metrics.label: Disk queue (avg requests)
metrics.description: Requests waiting or in service on the busiest device (iostat aqu-sz). Compare it with how many the device serves in parallel.

telegraf.note: milliseconds, one series per device (tag name): keep the device in the instance column

datadog.note: one series per device: export the max by host

otel.note: seconds, one series per device: keep the device in the instance column

cloudwatch.note: needs the CloudWatch agent; a count taken at each sample, not an average; statistic Maximum, per device (name)

metrics.name: filesystem.free.pct
metrics.label: Filesystem free (%)
metrics.description: Space left on the fullest filesystem, tmpfs and overlay left out. Logs, temp files and uploads fill a disk during a soak, and at 0 writes fail.

metrics.name: network.bytes.rate
metrics.label: Network throughput (B/s, rx+tx)
metrics.description: Bytes received and sent per second over every interface but loopback. Compare it with the link's or the instance type's bandwidth.

otel.note: both directions, every device but lo: export the sum per host

metrics.name: network.errors.rate
metrics.label: NIC errors + drops (/s)
metrics.description: Packets the interfaces dropped or received in error, per second: ring buffers overflowing under load, or a bad link. Drops also count frames the kernel discards for an unknown protocol, so a small steady rate can be healthy: compare it with an idle run.

metrics.name: tcp.retransmit.pct
metrics.label: TCP retransmits (% of segments sent)
metrics.description: Segments sent again, as a percentage of all segments sent: packet loss or congestion between the load generator, the application and its backends. Loss inflates tail latency long before throughput drops.

metrics.name: fd.used.pct
metrics.label: File handles used (%)
metrics.description: Open files system-wide, as a percentage of fs.file-max. A process's own limit (ulimit -n) usually bites first, so this one rarely moves.

metrics.name: context.switches.rate
metrics.label: Context switches (/s)
metrics.description: How often the kernel switched tasks, per second. A jump while throughput stays flat is time lost to the scheduler: too many threads for the cores.
